entries.title: Bears' grades are in. How did they do against the Lions?
entries.summary: <p>DETROIT — Any day now, our heads will stop spinning after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/26/bears-inactives-vs-lions-lt-theo-benedet-playing-cb-kyler-gordon-out" target="_blank" >the Bears’ 39-35 comeback win against the Lions</a> at Ford Field.</p><p>But right now? Holy wooziness, people. This isn't the onset of a tryptophan coma. It's the comedown from one of the wildest, tensest <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> finishes in memory, especially considering they had the big stage as the only NFL game going at the time. Hug your children. Sneak an extra nip from your brother-in-law's liquor cabinet. God bless America.</p><p>Let's get to the grades:</p><h3><b>QUARTERBACK — A-MINUS</b></h3><h3></h3><p>You want perfect? You’ve got the wrong guy. Caleb Williams took a completely unnecessary first-down sack at the Bears’ 2-yard line late in the second quarter, leading to his disastrous fumble and a safety on the next play. Twice, he appeared to miss receivers running free down the deep middle — once Luther Burden, later Zavion Thomas — checking down instead. A few times, he didn’t run for the sticks when it looked like he easily could. But who was that guy who dropped a feather into Rome Odunze’s hands for a 41-yard touchdown midway through the fourth? And ran for a first down on fourth-and-short with two minutes left? And laid one of the great throws of his career into the back corner of the end zone for a 6-yard Odunze touchdown with 0:03 on the clock? That was your QB. That was your guy. Count your blessings.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">THAT'S A TOUCHDOWN!!!!!!<br><br>📺: CBS <a href="https://t.co/IOUvYvWOHa">pic.twitter.com/IOUvYvWOHa</a></p>— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) <a href="https://x.com/ChicagoBears/status/2126065781351825530?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 26, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3><b>RUNNING BACKS — A</b></h3><p>OK, so D’Andre Swift is no Jahmyr Gibbs, but what do you want from him? Swift, a former Lion who wasn’t about to hold off Detroit’s best back since Barry Sanders, put in serious work for the visitors, rushing for 65 yards and a touchdown on only nine carries and piling up a career-high 97 receiving yards. And did you get a load of Salvon Ahmed, who clearly has too much juice to remain on the practice squad? That was some serious speed on his 46-yard run, and he showed excellent hands on his pair of catches. Kyle Monangai had two short runs for touchdowns.</p><h3><b>RECEIVERS — B</b></h3><p>Odunze — Thanksgiving legend? That’s a bit too much, but his fourth quarter — especially the money catch at the very end — goes right to the top of the Bears’ holiday highlight reel. Move the heck over, Dave Williams’ kickoff return to beat the Lions in overtime in 1980. Tight end Colston Loveland fumbled early and soon after was carted off with a knee injury, a crushing blow to a unit that already lost Cole Kmet, but Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson stepped up with a combined seven catches. Jahdae Walker should have held on to a desperation lollipop from Williams in the fourth, but couldn’t.</p><h3><b>RUN DEFENSE — F</b></h3><p>The Bears allowed 41 yards on 10 carries, which isn’t that terrible when you really think about it. Oops, sorry, almost forgot Gibbs’ 21 carries for 205 yards and three touchdowns. Good lord, that’s a day. Gibbs had a 70-yarder for a score. On an even better run that went for 32 yards, he broke free from defensive back Clark Phillips’ two-handed grasp behind the line of scrimmage on the right side of the field before circling all the way back around left end just like Sanders used to do. Is there a linebacker or a DB who can tackle in the house?</p><h3><b>PASS DEFENSE — D-PLUS</b></h3><p>It doesn’t help when there’s no pass rush to speak of, which was the case in this one. Pretty sure cornerbacks Malik Muhammad and Jaylon Johnson are still yanking on Amon-Ra St. Brown’s jersey, but it isn’t working. No, rookie safety Dillon Thieneman can’t run with speedy wideout Jameson Williams one-on-one; it’s a miracle Williams came up with only one big play, a 39-yard catch. But Thieneman had a huge interception off a deflection to keep the Bears in the hunt, and linebacker T.J. Edwards’ fourth-down stop of Gibbs after a catch gave the Bears one last possession — truly a gigantic play.</p><h3><b>BEN JOHNSON — GAME BALL</b></h3><p>He beat the team he came to the Bears from for the first time in five tries and ended up being hoisted in the air by his players in a raucous locker-room celebration. In between, his guys didn’t give up. That’s something, isn’t it?</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/26/bears-inactives-vs-lions-lt-theo-benedet-playing-cb-kyler-gordon-out" target="_blank" >Bears stun Lions 39-35 on QB Caleb Williams’ touchdown pass to Rome Odunze with 3 seconds left</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/26/bears-lions-colston-loveland-carted-to-locker-room-tight-end-thursday-ford-field" >Bears TE Colston Loveland carted off with knee injury</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>
